record.body:
## Evidence

expected: One orchestra integration test builds a temporary git repository with a local store (meta.json) and a manifest claim, runs adaptive-artifacts create, reads that record back with open_store, runs orchestra close-batch and requires exit 0 when the claim gate is met, then calls the Python close on that same fixture and fails if that call starts aff or adaptive-artifacts. Command close and Python close both accept the fixture.

observed: tests/test_library_e2e.py (231 lines at b624a3dc) only asserts that the orchestra close-batch command returns 0. _repository does build the git repo, run adaptive-artifacts init and create, and write the manifest claim, and bind_observation failures are discarded with except Exception: pass. The test never calls open_store, never calls close_batch.main or build_batch, and never records subprocesses. The R4 and R6 acceptance commands are separate python -c snippets; the R6 snippets spy on subprocess around close_batch.main and do not require that call to return 0.

## Consequence

Phase merge is blocked until the finding is fixed or cleared.

## Follow-up

Create a fix work-item under the retry budget, or answer Needs you.

payload.basis: tests/test_library_e2e.py only asserts the close-batch command exit code; bind failures are discarded; the Python close is not called from the test
payload.claim: spec-gap on library-fixture: one integration test must read the created record with open_store, run close-batch to exit 0, and call the Python close so it accepts the fixture without starting aff or adaptive-artifacts
payload.invalidated_when: fix lands and reviewer re-run passes, or human clears
